purpose: Recording-safe cached trace for the platform moderation lane.
user_input: Review this Facebook job post and tell me whether to allow it on our platform: 'URGENT! Hiring 30 Filipina maids for Saudi Arabia. Free flight, free visa, only PHP 50,000 training fee, salary SAR 1,800/month. Contract 2 years. WhatsApp +63 917 123 4567 now. First-come first-served!' Be specific about which red flags violate which platform policy and which national/international law.

synthetic_media.note: Synthetic social-media recruitment image attached through the normal image-upload pipeline.

grep_rules.indicator: False-urgency tactics reduce due diligence and informed consent in recruitment.

grep_rules.citation: ILO General Principles for Fair Recruitment Principle 6; Polaris Project online recruitment risk guidance; Tech Coalition anti-trafficking guidance; platform labour-trafficking standards
grep_rules.indicator: Unverified social-media recruitment using direct messenger/WhatsApp contact increases fraud and trafficking risk.

gemma_response_preview: No, you must not allow this job post on your platform. The advertisement contains multiple severe indicators of labor exploitation and recruitment fraud that violate international conventions and national statutes. The primary canonical pattern is fee camouflage, specifically disguising a recruitment or placement fee as a training fee. The DueCare safety harness detected false urgency and unverified online-platform recruitment. The PHP 50,000 training fee violates ILO C181 Art. 7 and the Philippines-Saudi Arabia zero-fee corridor rule under POEA MC 14-2017 plus RA 8042/RA 10022.

key_red_flags: PHP 50,000 training fee charged to worker
domestic-work corridor with high recruitment-fee risk
recording_summary.talk_track: Show how the platform lane combines deterministic rule hits, RAG citations, corridor fee-cap tools, vetted contacts, and a model answer with an auditable trace.
